Team — attaching a short redline (Redwood-Nimbus-DPA-v2-redline.pdf) and a one-page definitions doc (Telemetry-Definitions-20270423.docx). Summary of our positions below so Jasmine can communicate to Nimbus: 

1) Roles: Redwood accepts processor role for all customer-supplied input (prompts, files) and for the immediate outputs (generated text). For embeddings: we propose language that treats embeddings as "derived representations" of customer data. We will process embeddings as a processor; we will not re-use embeddings to train public models or for product-wide analytics unless the customer opts-in. Wording in redline: "Embeddings are treated as Customer Data and Processor will not use embeddings for model training or for improving model service unless the Customer provides explicit written consent."

2) Logs & Telemetry: we can commit to the following default controls:
- Retention: request-level logs containing prompt text are retained for 30 days by default for debugging; aggregated telemetry and system metrics retained longer (13 months) for reliability.
- Access: support and engineering access is role-based and logged; any access to request payloads requires an internal ticket with justification and is auditable.
- PII: we will flag PII in logs where possible and follow data minimization; recommend that Nimbus adopt client-side redaction for sensitive data if feasible.

3) Subprocessors: provide current list in the attachment; we offer 30 days' notice prior to onboarding new subprocessors, with a right for Nimbus to object in writing.

4) E-sign: we are happy to proceed via DocuSign. We'll prepare the final signed copy once Nimbus confirms the redline or provides a counter-redline.

If everyone agrees, Jasmine can send the redline to Nimbus' DPO and include the DocuSign prep link.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Head of Legal Operations (Privacy L2), Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
